chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, some people came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) after they had embraced Islam, and they said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Will a man from us be held accountable for what he did during the period of Ignorance after his Islam?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to them: 'The one whose Islam is good and the certainty of his faith is sound, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will not hold him accountable for what he did during the period of Ignorance; and the one whose Islam is shallow and the certainty of his faith is not sound, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will hold him accountable for the former and the latter.'
ai.seo_question: Does Islam forgive all sins committed before conversion?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the theological principle that the validity of faith (yaqin) determines whether pre-Islamic sins are forgiven or carried over, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding the status of early converts. It distinguishes between superficial conversion and deep, certain belief, implying that insincerity renders one accountable for both past and present deeds. This narration underscores the importance of internal conviction over mere external declaration in the process of spiritual purification.
